claim.quote: Here we report spectroscopy of a pure antimatter atom, demonstrating resonant quantum transitions in antihydrogen.

key_value_text.quote: we detect 23 atoms that survive in 110 trapping attempts with microwaves off-resonance (0.21 per attempt), and only two atoms that survive in 103 attempts with microwaves on-resonance (0.02 per attempt)
key_value_text.value: 23 survivors in 110 attempts off-resonance versus 2 in 103 attempts on-resonance

name: Resonant quantum transitions in trapped antihydrogen atoms

significance.quote: (0.21 per attempt), and only two atoms that survive in 103 attempts with microwaves on-resonance (0.02 per attempt)
significance.value: Survival rate 0.21 per attempt off-resonance versus 0.02 per attempt on-resonance (no sigma level stated in the abstract)

summary.plain: ALPHA used microwaves to flip the spin of the positron in trapped antihydrogen atoms and ejected them from the trap. Fewer atoms survived when the microwaves were on resonance than off resonance, showing resonant quantum transitions in antihydrogen.
summary.technical: Microwave spin-flip spectroscopy between hyperfine levels of trapped antihydrogen: in one variant, 23 atoms survived 110 trapping attempts with microwaves off-resonance (0.21 per attempt) and two atoms survived 103 attempts on-resonance (0.02 per attempt).

title: Resonant quantum transitions in trapped antihydrogen atoms
why_it_matters: The abstract frames it as spectroscopy of a pure antimatter atom, allowing comparison with hydrogen and a test of the validity of CPT symmetry.
